claim: A group admitting an injective rank-metric ultraproduct representation over finite fields of one fixed characteristic p has stably finite group algebra over every coefficient field of characteristic p.
quantifiers: For every prime p, countable group G, ultrafilter omega, finite fields F_i with char(F_i)=p on an omega-large set, dimensions n_i tending to infinity along omega, and injective homomorphism G -> prod_omega GL_n_i(F_i)/d_omega; for every field K with char(K)=p, K[G] is stably finite.
proof: For each finite k0=F_{p^d}, extend coordinate fields to L_i containing both F_i and k0, then restrict scalars to k0. Normalized rank is preserved exactly. Apply Arzhantseva-Paunescu Theorem 7.4 to embed k0[G] in a rank ultraproduct and Proposition 2.8 for stable finiteness. A hypothetical matrix one-sided inverse over arbitrary K gives a finite polynomial system over F_p, augmented by Z times one nonzero group coefficient of BA-I equal to 1. A maximal ideal of its nonzero finite-type coordinate algebra has finite residue field by Zariski's lemma, contradicting stable finiteness over that finite extension k0.

costs.restriction_of_scalars: N_i=n_i[L_i:k0], where L_i=F_{p^lcm(d,e_i)}; normalized rank is exact, but [L_i:k0] can be unbounded.
costs.AP_amplification: The source's displayed construction uses matrix dimension n_i^i*2^i at stage i; no efficiency is claimed.
costs.witness_specialization: For fixed matrix size r, one variable per coefficient in the finite supports of the entries of A and B, plus one inverse-defect variable; the residue degree has no bound here.

strongest_baseline: Sofic groups satisfy direct finiteness over every field by Elek-Szabo. AP already proves fixed-field rank-model -> group-algebra embedding and stable finiteness; this proof extends the interface to varying finite fields of one characteristic and all coefficient fields of that characteristic.
falsifier: A checked matrix one-sided inverse over a same-characteristic coefficient field for a group satisfying the stated rank-model premise would contradict either the restriction-of-scalars identity, AP's embedding, or the finite-field specialization proof.
scope: This does not produce a fixed-characteristic rank model from hyperlinearity or from a complex linear-sofic model. The group-level implication remains conditional on the supplied model.

claim: Failure of direct finiteness of K[G] over any field K of characteristic p yields failure over some finite extension F_{p^d}.
quantifiers: For arbitrary group G, field K of characteristic p, and finitely supported a,b in K[G] with ab=1 and ba!=1.
proof: Treat coefficients of a,b as variables over F_p; impose all coefficient equations for ab=1 and add Z D_u=1 for a nonzero coefficient D_u of ba-1. The resulting finite-type coordinate algebra is nonzero because K supplies a solution. A maximal ideal has finite residue field over F_p by Zariski's lemma, and the residue classes give the same one-sided inverse witness.
falsifier: A one-sided inverse witness over K whose finite polynomial system had no finite residue-field point would contradict Zariski's lemma.

costs.equations: Coefficient equations on the finite product supports of ab and ba, plus one equation forcing a chosen defect coefficient nonzero.
costs.degree_bound: No bound on the degree d of the finite residue field is derived.

scope: This is a reduction of a hypothetical witness, not a direct-finiteness theorem by itself.

claim: A fixed finite complex rank model reduces to a finite field of prescribed characteristic p while preserving a finite list of ranks whenever the product c of selected nonzero maximal minors is not nilpotent modulo pR.
quantifiers: For a finite list of matrices over a finitely generated Z-subalgebra R of C, including chosen generator inverses, multiplicativity defects, and nonidentity separation matrices; choose a maximal nonzero minor for each positive-rank matrix and let c be their product.
proof: The condition c not in sqrt(pR) says (R/pR)[1/c] is nonzero. A maximal ideal of this finite-type F_p algebra yields a finite residue field; the rank minors selected remain nonzero while all larger minors vanish identically in R. Including inverse entries preserves invertibility after reduction.

costs.matrix_list: O(|E|+|E|^2) matrices of size n for a finite set E.
costs.arithmetic: Requires exact coefficients, rank-minor selection, and ideal/specialization work; no uniform bit-height or runtime bound is given.

falsifier: A reduction under the stated condition that changes the rank of one listed matrix would contradict the maximal-minor argument.
scope: The condition can fail for a chosen model; this does not rule out a different model over the prescribed prime.

claim: Each fixed finite complex rank-model stage over a characteristic-zero finite-type domain is p-safe for all but finitely many primes, but this stagewise fact does not guarantee one prime is safe eventually along a sequence.
proof: For a fixed stage, R[1/c] is a nonzero finite-type domain over Z. The image of Spec(R[1/c]) -> Spec(Z) is constructible and contains the generic point, hence contains all but finitely many prime points. The exact Z model theta_k(m)=diag(P_k^m,...,P_k^{km}) for P_k the product of the first k primes has coefficient ring Z[1/P_k]; each fixed prime is a unit at every sufficiently late stage, so no coordinate reduction to that fixed characteristic exists there.
quantifiers: The cofinite assertion is per fixed stage. The sequence counterexample is a selected model of Z, not a statement that Z lacks models in any characteristic.
falsifier: A fixed finite-type characteristic-zero domain with nonzero c whose fibers c!=0 are empty for infinitely many prime characteristics would contradict constructibility of the dominant image.
scope: Z is sofic and has another rank model over every F_p via prime-length permutation cycles; the counterexample is to model-specific specialization only.

claim: One complete r=s=t=2 Cartesian triangle block admits an exact incidence-dependent GL_D(F_q) assignment with every nondegenerate rectangle W=-I_D and rank(I-W)=D for every odd q and every D>=1.
quantifiers: For i=(alpha,beta) in Z/2 x Z/2, u,v in {1,2}, set all L=I_D; set R_(1,0)=R_(1,1)=R_(2,0)=I_D and R_(2,1)=-I_D; define X_iuv=R_(v,beta+u mod 2).
proof: Every triangle is I*R*R^{-1}=I. For beta=0 the X array is [[I,-I],[I,I]], and for beta=1 it is [[I,I],[I,-I]]. The ordered rectangle cross ratio is -I or its inverse, equal to -I. Since q is odd, I-(-I)=2I has full rank. The local block sum has rank exactly D.

costs.construction: Four i indices, 16 scalar-block X slots, and eight L/R slots; constant-size exact arithmetic for D=1.
costs.verification: Independent exact checker covers q=3,7 and D=1,2; all-D/all-odd-q claim follows symbolically from scalar multiples of I_D.

falsifier: Any failure among the 16 triangle equations or any ordered rectangle with rank(I-W)<D falsifies the displayed assignment.
scope: Refutes local triangle-only incompatibility. It does not extend to N65 globally because each X_iuv is shared across all incidence blocks of label i and the global interpolation identities couple those blocks.

claim: A faithful normalized-HS ultraproduct representation can have multiplicativity defects that converge to zero in HS norm but have full rank at every finite stage.
example: For irrational alpha/(2pi), theta_n(m)=exp(i(alpha*m+c(m)/n))I_n on Z, with c(0)=0 and c(m)=1 for m!=0. The model is injective in HS metric ultraproduct, while theta_n(1)^2-theta_n(2) is a nonzero scalar multiple of I_n for every n.
scope: Refutes generic HS-small => rank-small conversion only. It does not rule out another representation or a more structured conversion. Full derivation is in the Cycle 4 positive-characteristic model-transfer leaf.
